The code sets X = X.mT and then computes R = X @ X.mT. When the original G is transposed (m > n), X becomes n x m with n < m. The code correctly enters the rectangular branch (m > n) and computes R = X @ X.mT which is n x n. However, the final output is computed as X = X.mT @ Q.mT. Here X.mT is m x n, Q is n x n, so X.mT @ Q.mT is m x n. But this result has shape m x n, whereas the expected output should have shape n x m (i.e., the transposed back). The code attempts to transpose back, but the multiplication order is wrong: it should be Q @ X.mT to yield n x m, or equivalently X.mT @ Q.mT only if X.mT were m x n and Q were m x m. In the rectangular branch, Q is n x n (since R is n x n). The correct formula is Q @ X.mT (n x n @ m x n = n x m). The current code produces X.mT @ Q.mT which is m x n, a shape mismatch and numerically wrong. This will cause shape errors or silently wrong updates for any parameter with more rows than columns (common for transformer weight matrices). Trigger: any call to muon_update with a 2D grad where grad.size(-2) > grad.size(-1) and ns_method=\"gram\".
